description: Composite fracture-surface figure of three Charpy impact specimens — (a) S1000, (b) S1050 and (c) MHT — each panel combining a high-magnification secondary-electron SEM fractograph with a small low-magnification "reduction map" inset (yellow border, 1 mm scale bar) in the lower-left corner that outlines the shear zone with a yellow dashed line. (a) (5 µm scale bar) shows flat quasi-cleavage planes (white arrow "Quasi-cleavage"), microvoids (yellow/orange arrows "Microvoids"), a microcrack (green arrow "Microcrack"), a red dashed line tracing an apparent grain boundary and a red dashed ellipse marking a microvoid. (b) (10 µm scale bar) shows similar quasi-cleavage with striated slip bands, labelled "Microcrack" and "Microvoids". (c) (10 µm scale bar) is a fully dimpled surface, with "Dimple" labelled by a white arrow and no quasi-cleavage plane. Reading the insets together, the shear zone (yellow dashed outline) enlarges progressively from S1000 to S1050 to MHT, the visual counterpart of the caption/citing-text claim that larger shear-zone area correlates with better toughness and a quasi-cleavage-to-ductile fracture transition.

observations.observation: The figure is a three-panel composite of SEM impact-fracture surfaces labelled (a) S1000, (b) S1050 and (c) MHT, each containing a low-magnification fractograph inset with a yellow border.
Panel (a) (S1000) carries the printed labels 'Microcrack' (green arrow), 'Quasi-cleavage' (white arrow) and 'Microvoids' (yellow/orange arrows) at a 5 µm scale bar.
In panel (a) a red dashed line is drawn over the surface and a red dashed ellipse encloses a microvoid, as stated in the citing text for the S1000 grain-boundary marking.
Panel (b) (S1050) shows a quasi-cleavage plane with parallel slip-band striations plus a labelled microcrack (green arrow) and microvoids (orange arrows), at a 10 µm scale bar.
Panel (c) (MHT) shows a dimpled, ductile fracture surface with 'Dimple' labelled by a white arrow at a 10 µm scale bar and no quasi-cleavage plane.
Each low-magnification inset has a 1 mm scale bar and a yellow dashed outline delimiting a shear zone on the fracture surface.
The caption states the low-magnification insets are reduction maps with a yellow border.
The citing text states the shear zone areas of S1000, S1050 and MHT gradually increase and that a larger shear zone area corresponds to better toughness.
The citing text attributes the slip bands on the quasi-cleavage plane to large numbers of dislocations moving along the quasi-cleavage plane.
The citing text states microcracks and microvoids occur where slip-band interaction is significant, and that S1000 shows an intergranular fracture character along the marked grain boundary.
The citing text states the MHT sample has more dimples and no microcracks and no quasi-cleavage plane, i.e. a ductile fracture.

subfigures.description: SEM impact-fractograph of S1000 (5 µm scale bar): flat quasi-cleavage planes (white arrow), microvoids (yellow/orange arrows), a microcrack (green arrow); a red dashed line marks an apparent grain boundary and a red dashed ellipse marks a microvoid. Lower-left inset is the low-magnification reduction map (yellow border, 1 mm scale bar) with the shear zone outlined in yellow dashed line.

SEM impact-fractograph of S1050 (10 µm scale bar): quasi-cleavage plane with parallel slip-band striations (white arrow), a microcrack (green arrow) and microvoids (orange arrows). Lower-left inset is the low-magnification reduction map (1 mm scale bar) with the yellow-dashed shear zone, larger than in (a).

SEM impact-fractograph of MHT (10 µm scale bar): fully dimpled ductile fracture surface, 'Dimple' labelled with a white arrow; no quasi-cleavage plane visible. Lower-left inset is the low-magnification reduction map (1 mm scale bar) showing the largest yellow-dashed shear zone of the three specimens.
